utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I just remind you, General, of the affirmation taken at the commencement of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all. Can we have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P118 from the Jokic binder, tab 18. My apologies, Your Honour. The mistake is all mine. I'm talking about tab 19. That's the following exhibit in the Jokic binder, Exhibit Number 119. My apologies again, Your Honours, for this mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, if I'm not mistaken, you referred to this document in your expert report, And there are several references to it in your footnotes. This document, decision on further activities of the command of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 24th of October, 1991. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at item 2, units of the 2nd Operational Group. After carrying out the combat activities, the 9th VPS and 472nd Motorised Brigade units reach the line, and then the line they reached is given, in terms of the villages they reached, the third unit of the 2nd Operational Group. Isn't that right? Yes or no, general?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at item 3, the last sentence in it of the first passage of item 3. Is it true that the commander of the 2nd OG hereby issues an order to prevent any attacks against the old part of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in the third -- under item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now look at the next passage following that sentence. If ones looks at the passage, does it not indicate that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group requests the commander of the 9th VPS and 472nd Motorised Brigade report to him personally on the 25th of October, 1991 with a draft decision on the forces gathering at the line that had been reached? Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember, on Friday you were shown Defence Exhibit D43. That is a decision by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 25th of October, 1991 for the 472nd Motorised Brigade to be to its original unit within the 9th VPS. Do you remember looking at that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that I was submitted this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That sort of decision by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, would it not be a result of a proposal that came from his subordinate commanders regarding the grouping of forces as indicated by the decision that you currently have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't know whether I understood the question. The decision of the commander of the 2nd OG was issued even before he invited his subordinates to report. And on the 24th, he called them for the 25th, to report. I wonder whether I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a decision on further activities by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 24th of October. What it refers to is the work and activities to be undertaken by the unit on the following day, the 25th of October. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For further actions, not -- refers to all further actions, not only the next day. But they can be also corrected for each subsequent day. That is also true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That decision, item 3 of that decision, this passage, it is requested that the following day, the commanders of the 9th VPS and the 472 Motorised Brigade, that is on the 25th of October, should come to see him about -- with a proposal on the grouping of the forces at the line reached.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. After -- on the 24th, both commanders accepted this assignment. They have to prepare the decisions. And with that decision, come on the 25th of October to the command post of the 2nd OG and to report to their superiors prior to continuation of other combat operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question: The decision by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 25th of October, 1991 the one that you saw on Friday, which states that the 472nd Motorised Brigade should return to its original unit within the 9th VPS, that decision -- could that decision be a result of this task that was assigned to these commanders by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group; namely, to come and see him, bringing with him a proposal on how the forces should be grouped. Would that not be a logical sequence of events?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 24th of October, the 472nd VPS [as interpreted] was not under the command of the 9th VPS, but it was directly under the command of the 2nd OG. After reporting on their decisions on the 25th of October, the commander of the 2nd OG could accept this change. And on the 25th of October, resubordinate this unit to the 9th VPS. This is not an outcome of the decision of the 24th, but it is an outcome of the situation on the battle front on the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. There is a transcript error. Page 4, line 9, it reads: "472nd VPS," and I believe it should read "brigade." Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, sir, does it not say the outcome of the situation on the front and a proposal on the grouping of the forces that this is what the commanders of the 9th VPS and the 472nd Motorised Brigade should report to the commander of 9th VPS about on the 25th in the morning when they were supposed to report at his command post?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of item 3, he indicated that both of the commanders should come at 0900 hours, 25th of October, and report their proposals of decisions -- of their own decisions [as interpreted]. And this always occurs prior to battle operations. Only after that, the two commanders can issue decisions to their subordinates. Therefore, from this, it does not result -- from the document, it doesn't result that anything has changed in the battle positions. But of course, they -- it might have changed during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness Defence Exhibit D43. You can leave it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you understand my question now? The decision by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 25th of October for the 472nd Motorised Brigade to return to the composition of its original 9th VPS; namely, that this was a result of the proposal he had received from the commanders of the 9th VPS and the 472nd Motorised Brigade at the briefing, as he had ordered them in his previous decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has been asked and answered. I think that this is rehashing a question that has been addressed by the witness just moments ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be, but I'm not sufficiently informed at the moment in the evidence whether that is the case or not. So I must allow Mr. Rodic to proceed with this question, at least this one further time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. There was just one problem we had. The witness was answering my questions about the operations carried out on the front, and my question was actually only about the grouping of the forces, about whether the return of that particular unit to its original 9th VPS composition would be part of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. regrouping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regrettably, I -- grouping of forces in Serbo-Croatian, I didn't maybe get it right. The decision on the grouping of forces does not imply analysis and resubordination and reattachment to forces where he orders them to prepare a proposal of decision for force grouping. He did not decide -- issue a decision on any changes of the chain of command. And he cannot request that from his subordinates. So that's the first. Secondly - and I emphasise - any reorganisation of command and control is always the result of the battle situation. Of course, both commanders at 9.00 p.m., when they were briefing the commander of the 2nd OG, maybe they were proposing something like that. I do not know. But that is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now show the witness an OTP exhibit. It's P101 from the Jokic binder, tab 3. That's the entire binder as it pertains to Witness Jokic. General Zorc, do you have in front of you a decision by the commander, or rather a combat order of the commander of the 9th VPS dated the 20th November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20th? Yes. I heard the 20th. Yes, the 20th of November, 1991. Battle order number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at item 1, the first sentence. How do you interpret that first sentence? What actually happened within the composition of the 9th VPS, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From item 1 of this battle order of the commander of the 9th VPS, it arises that on the basis of the decision of the commander of the 2nd OG for the 19th of November, 1991, the 472nd Motorised Brigade be newly resubordinated from the military naval district and be subordinated directly to the command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rather, as it is stated in the brackets, the 2nd Corps. Does that mean that perhaps it's being subordinated to the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states that it will operate on the basis of command of the 2nd Operational Group, the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown -- rather, before we start --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a look at this document when you made your report?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't believe that I've seen this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now please be shown Exhibit P1, which is also a binder from the Jokic binder, tab 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, this is a document from the command of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 5th of February, 1992. The document was sent to SSNO to the General Staff of the armed forces and to the First Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but it looks like the transcript is not moving. Is yours reflecting the same stagnant condition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There has been no movement. Whether we've failed or whether there is a -- some other type of problem ... Could the court officer make inquiries, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Something is happening now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May we ask that the exhibit number be put on the record that's being referred to. I'm afraid that did not make it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the exhibit number, Mr. Rodic, that you're having the witness look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I requested and what the witness has been shown is OTP Exhibit P102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, do you have in front of you a document of the command of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 5th of February, 1992, which bespeaks the composition of the forces in terms of which unit they belonged to within the system of command and control of the JNA of the Territorial Defence and the volunteers unit. It's a document that was sent to the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, or rather the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the SFRY. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now look at the second page of this document under item 5, the Boka VPS. On the 5th of February, 1992, within the composition of the 9th VPS, was there not also the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall no longer be requiring this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, tell us, please, was every high-ranking officer responsible for the units under his command and all commanders under his command would have been responsible for the respective units under their command, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. That is what I have also explained in previous questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In terms of carrying out the respective command responsibilities, is it true that command responsibility is implemented through the giving of orders to one's subordinate commanders through monitoring the implementation of those orders and through a system of reporting in that regard to him as the superior commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. And we should add also that assistance to the subordinate units in the carrying out of their assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, when you saw these documents, whose duty was it between the 25th of October and the 21st of November, 1991 at the first level of command responsibility to control the 472nd Motorised Brigade? Who was in charge of that unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At present, I don't have in front of me the documents we reviewed previously. But if it's for the period when this brigade was again resubordinated to the 9th VPS, then at the time the commander of the 9th VPS was responsible for them. But as I said, I don't have the documents with the precise date in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to remind you of the following: You looked at Document D43, a decision by the command of the 2nd Operational Group for the 472nd Motorised Brigade to rejoin the composition of the 9th VPS on the 25th of October. And you also saw the combat order of the 9th VPS dated the 20th of November, which indicates that the 472nd Motorised Brigade without the 3rd Battalion should be detached from the composition of the 9th VPS. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then tell me, sir, whose duty was it in that period of time at the first level of command responsibility to keep under control the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an open question. If the command of the 9th VPS is also at the time when the remaining part of the 472nd Motorised Brigade was reinstated, and if it retained the direct command over the 3rd Battalion, then it commanded it directly. But if the 3rd Battalion, which was prior in the 9th VPS composition, if it was resubordinated to the brigade, then for that battalion, the brigade commander was responsible for them. However, I have not seen a document which would be regulating this issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. Tell us, please, sir, between the 21st of November, 1991 and the 5th of February, 1992 - you looked at those documents, didn't you? - who was responsible for the first level of command responsibility in terms of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. controlling the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the documents we considered, the 3rd Battalion remained under the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, sir, please, the commander of the 9th VPS in actual fact, did he exercise control over the 472nd Motorised Brigade as the documents that you looked at seem to indicate and as the documents apparently led you to believe while you were writing your report?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as any document concerning effectiveness of command of that brigade while it was subordinate to the 9th VPS, I did not have at my disposal. However, the command of the 9th VPS commanded and commanded this unit as it did with other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of the 9th VPS, did he exercise control over the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. And it was under his subordination throughout this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, sir, if the commander of the 9th VPS is unhappy about the 472nd Motorised Brigade and the 3rd Battalion because their performance is poor and they lack discipline and for this reason he refuses to go and visit those units for the duration of their direct subordination to him, thereby ignoring them and showing clearly what he thinks about them, that sort of behaviour by the commander of the 9th VPS, would that be in compliance with the doctrine of command such as you know it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This in no case it can be in line with the doctrine of command and control. Quite the opposite. If the commander is dissatisfied with the behaviour, the conduct, and performance with one of its subordinate units, he must dedicate all his attention to these units or this unit, and also personally supervise it. I believe supervise it personally means by his personal presence in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever come across a situation like that when you looked at Admiral Jokic's interview? I'm referring to the interview that you used for your report. When I say "Admiral Jokic's interview" I mean the one dated September 2003.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have stated, I have not studied this interview. I browsed through it. And from this interview, if my memory -- if my recollection is correct, the sector commander was not satisfied with the situation, and the operations of the 472nd Motorised Brigade and its 3rd Battalion. Primarily, he was not satisfied with the activities of certain officers and the commander of the 3rd Battalion and the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, you used those problems as conclusions in your report, and you inferred that Admiral Jokic, at least based on the interview that you saw, had encountered problems and that he had asked for the resignation of some of the officers. Isn't that what you state in your report?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will read out to you the portion of that interview on page 95, the B/C/S version; in English, that would be page 103. The investigator's question is as follows: "It strikes me as logical that you are on the front, but what does not strike me as logical is that you took the 3rd Light Brigade and not the elements of the 472nd Brigade which you knew you had problems with." And the answer of Miodrag Jokic was: "This may be a personal position. I never went to the command post of that brigade. That's one thing I admit." Furthermore, I'll show you another passage on page 96 of the B/C/S, and we're still on page 103 of the English. The passage reads: "Miodrag Jokic says: `I thought they were so bad, I thought the situation was so bad that this was my way of showing how I felt about them.'" In addition to which the brigade in practical terms was not engaged in any operation at the time. It was the 3rd Battalion. The investigator's question: "Why, then, did you not go to its 3rd Battalion?" Answer by Miodrag Jokic: "Well, the commander lieutenant general does not go to a battalion. He could get killed the moment he arrives. If you send someone to a battalion, then sometimes you send a brigade commander at best." What I've just quoted from Miodrag Jokic's interview, does that tally in terms of the doctrine of command with the kind of behaviour that a corps commander should display towards his subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say. I couldn't state that. He was supposed to be personally involved in places where certain questions and issues arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I suppose you didn't use this particular section of the interview when writing up your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. As far as the attitude of commanders towards certain units or reserve or active forces, I didn't write about that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I've just shown you, that sort of behaviour of the commander of the 9th VPS, can that be viewed as responsible behaviour on the part of any commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. But as I already stated, I don't think we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, General Zorc, please, you were a corps commander. You as a commander, would you not go more frequently to undisciplined units to your subordinate commanders, or would you go more often to the good units and the good and disciplined commanders?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regrettably, the assignments of the commanding officer are such that he must be involved there where he might least want to be. It would be, of course, nice to be visiting always the good units. But you have to focus on the problematic units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell me, sir, this sort of attitude by the commander of the 9th VPS, what about the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade? Do you think he could understand that as some form of encouragement or support to the sort of control and behaviour that he was involved in at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, that's speculative, Your Honour. Inasmuch as the predicate underlying it is that there wasn't even a visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question itself is speculative, Mr. Rodic. But you are asking whether a failure of a commander of an operational group to visit a unit ever might be regarded as approval of the conduct of the group, rather than asking specifically particulars. And I don't know whether the general can help us with that general proposition. Would a failure of the commander of an operational group ever to visit a battalion be interpreted or could it reasonably be interpreted as approval of that battalion's conduct?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, my question was about the commander of the 9th VPS. That's what the question referred to. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. Rodic. Yes. The commander of the...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it please the Court, such an exceptional situation can, in fact, lead to such undesirable impressions and conclusions on the part of a subordinated commander. Perhaps not really in the context that his superior fully approves of the actions of the subordinate commander, but it can be interpreted in the context that the commander has nothing against it or that he doesn't care. As I stated for a similar case in my report, I cannot claim that the superior commander wanted his subordinate to get such an impression. However, the subordinate commander who was left to himself could have understood this course of action in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, when you wrote your report, did you find any written evidence that Admiral Jokic had requested the removal of the commander of the Chief of Staff of the 472nd Motorised Brigade and the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't remember seeing that anywhere in written form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then tell me what is the reason that you believe the words of Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic, what he said in the interview, when he claimed that he had asked for the removal of those officers if, based Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on some of the previous questions, when I showed you an interview concerning his behaviour towards that brigade and that specific battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, the questions or the documents, in fact, which you presented to me about the fact that the VPS commander had such an attitude as he towards his subordinate unit, I never saw that information earlier. The only information that I did have was from his interview stating that he was unhappy with those units and that he proposed those officers to be replaced. That is why I accepted that opinion as a basis for my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, in your report, there are at least four or five references to conclusions that you reach based on Admiral Jokic's interview to the investigators in September 2003. What I want to know is was there may be someone from the OTP who, when they gave you the task to write your report, only provided some sections of the interview and not some others, or did they give you the entire interview for you to go through and study?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing of the sort happened. It is true, as I mentioned, that I received this interview, and I frisked through it in a rapid manner. And as I browsed through the interview, I got information on the attitude of the 9th VPS commander towards the 3rd Battalion. But my insight into the document was neither directed nor limited in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Tell me, please, and I must ask you this, do you know Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic personally? Are you perhaps friends?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Admiral Jokic personally. I know him from our time together in the highest level of military schools. But that is the extent of our knowledge of one another. I could not say that we are friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apology.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, if you allow me, I don't want this to be misinterpreted, we were colleagues, we attended school together. We shared a life during the school. But after those school days, we did not have any contacts, just to prevent any misunderstanding. It is also true that I had a very good opinion of Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, when you read Admiral Jokic's interview dated September 2003, did you perhaps come across a section of the interview where he makes reference to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 92 of the B/C/S version of the interview, which is on page 99 of the English, the investigator asks the following question: "But Colonel Marinovic, for example, resigned, and then Milovan Zorc," that's a reference to you. And the answer by Jokic is: "No, no, no. That's now how it was." Investigator: "I have not finished with this yet. The Sarajevo Corps in May 1992, the man there, also resigned unhappy about the political developments and he was afraid he would not be able to effectively exercise control over his unit." And the answer by Jokic was: "No, no, that was no resignation. As for Zorc, I know because I was his schoolmate." Is that the answer you found also?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see this in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, General, on page 21 of your report, your expert report, you say that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group often had direct contact with the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade. Can you tell me where these frequent contacts took place and where they were held -- where and when they were held?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this piece of information also stems from the interview, the interview with General Jokic -- Admiral Jokic. And that it was contacts at the level of the 2nd OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the documents and in the material that were shown to you, apart from this interview, when you were writing your report, did you find anything that would lead to any such thing, like what Vice Admiral Jokic said?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not come across anything of the nature. These were not formal contacts; these were informal contacts. And such informal contacts are possible. It would also be possible to have formal contacts between two commanders from two different levels of command. That would be possible. This did not, however, have any influences on the systemic questions on which I was asked to look into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that particular conclusion, you also said that the officers from the command of the 2nd Operational Group were stationed in that battalion, the 3rd Battalion. Can you tell me which officers from the command of the 2nd Operational Group were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't give you names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know, then, that officers from the 2nd Operational Group were stationed there in the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came across this in a document where it was stated that along with officers from the 9th VPS, individual units also received for a certain time, for certain actions, officers from the command of the 2nd OG. And that would not be abnormal at all. However, I'm afraid I can't remember where I saw that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, if in fact what counsel has asked the witness is supposedly a direct quotation, line 16 of page 18: "In that particular conclusion, you also said that the officers in the command of the 2nd Operational Group were stationed in that battalion, that their battalion," what I'm looking -- what it says is: "Furthermore, on the Dubrovnik front" -- this page 23 in the English version. "On the Dubrovnik front some combat units and their commands were deployed within relative proximity of a command post or of a forward command post of the 2nd operations [sic] group which enabled officers and commanding officers of the 2nd operations group to be present in person in the subordinate commands and in some battalions." That is not as the question was posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, nevertheless, I was interested in where the witness got this kind of information and how come it became part of his report. That is what I wish to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, at least in the interview, if not in other documents, did you come across the names of the officers from the 9th VPS that were specifically in charge of supervising the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I do not recall which document contains this information and which officers these were. As I remember, this was the commander of the artillery, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown a document, a Defence document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, I would like to ask the usher to have D65 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, do you remember having seen this document already on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in the introduction of the document reference is made to officers. Does this speak in a positive sense of the courage and dedication of the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, specifically the name is Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is stated here that this is an extremely capable and courageous officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document is sent, as we said, to the head of the operations group of the General Staff of the SFRY, General Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you the following: In the system of command and control, does there have to be mutual trust among commanders and officers?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. That is very much desirable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when you wrote your report, after that particular date, the 6th of December, 1991, did you see any documents or did you see any piece of information stating that a replacement was sought for the commander of the 3rd Battalion, that Vice Admiral Jokic asked for him to be removed?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already mentioned, I do not recall which document I saw this information in. I presume that this information stems from his interview. I don't remember the document itself. I may have seen a document to this effect, but I did not use it, nor did I quote it as a source for my report. I suppose if I did have such a concrete document, I would certainly have referred to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you perhaps come across a piece of information in any document that the commander of the 9th VPS issued an order to the commander of the 3rd Battalion that he should be relieved of his post, any such thing, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not come across any such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, a corps commander, specifically, the commander of the 9th VPS which holds such a rank, can in a particular case initiate proceedings to remove the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade who is directly subordinated to him?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can submit such a proposal to his superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether you found out through documents or in any other way that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group went to report to the federal secretary for national defence, General Kadijevic, on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That he would have had to report to him, no. That would mean that he was called on in disciplinary terms. I did not come across any information of this nature. However, I did find in the documentation that the commander of the 2nd OG and the commander of the 9th VPS were called to see the federal secretary. I did not come across any reason why they were called to see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, this is the 6th of December, 1991 that is in question. I assume that you received the indictment and read it when you wrote your report. As you read the interview of Admiral Jokic, did you come across this particular piece of information, that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and Vice Admiral Jokic as commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector on that day, the 6th of December, 1991, and in relation to what was going on around Dubrovnik and the operations of units there were called in to come to see him in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I suppose I saw this in the interview with Admiral Jokic. I did not come across the reasons why they were called on, but I suppose that they were called on because of their combat activities around Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, within the 2nd Operational Group as an establishment covering a particular territory with its own units deployed within its area of responsibility, whose area of responsibility and operations was the territory of the town of Dubrovnik and its surroundings? Whose units were in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the blockade of Dubrovnik, units under the 9th VPS command participated in the actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the units of the 9th VPS? Did they take part in this, both from land and sea in the blockade of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, naval forces also participated in the blockade from the maritime side. Those units, too, came from the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you wrote your report -- actually, I would like to know what you know about the 6th of December and what actually happened on the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, that's likely to lead to a fairly long answer. I know it's a little early, but would it be convenient to break now and deal with that afterward?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, before the break, I put a question in relation to what you know about the information you have concerning the 6th of December, 1991 and developments there and then, the 6th of December, 1991. If you can tell me briefly of the information that you have.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you could see from my report, concrete questions were put to me, and these questions were related to the system of command and control and responsibilities and competencies of the military officers for the activities of their units. As far as the incident on the 6th of December, 1991 is concerned, my information is only about the fact that on that day the old city of Dubrovnik was shelled, protected as a cultural monument. As to the scope of action, the way in which it was conducted, the scope of damages or anything else concerning these concrete events on that day were not of relevance from the point of view of my report, and also I was not acquainted with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When reading the interview of Admiral Jokic from September 2003, did you find an explanation there why on the 6th of December the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector went to see General Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That shelling took place on the 6th of December, that is the information I got from the interview by Jokic. However, regrettably, I have to say again that I did not conclude from this that the shelling itself was the reason for them to go -- to be called in to see the Secretary-General of People's Defence. I concluded that there were some other reasons as well, and not only because of the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do accept certainly that the reason why they went there was what happened on the 6th of December, what had to do with the shelling of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, if I knew when they heard about the requirement of the Secretary-General, it would be easier for me to assess the reasons for it. If they were called in after the shelling started or was initiated, at least, then it is highly probable or then obviously, in fact, going to see him and talking about this incident could not be avoided by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, General Zorc. I'm not going to assert anything. But I would like to ask you in relation to the following questions that I have to take into account an assumption. Could you please take into account when giving these answers that will follow an assumption that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and the commander of the 9th VPS were called in to Belgrade on the 6th of December, 1991 because they were asked to do so by General Kadijevic, federal secretary of national defence. After he received information that Dubrovnik was being shelled. In that case, can General Kadijevic directly issue orders apart from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group to the commander of the 9th VPS because what was taking place was happening in his area of responsibility? Can he ask him to give him a report in writing about the incident itself, about the damages sustained, and in general the effects of what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The federal secretary is in fact a superior in the chain of command and can thus ask of anybody from the top down in the chain of command for activities that he wants to see performed. And first of all, he would ask for an immediate stopping of illegal actions and also for an accurate report about what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you have before you, or rather if you have in front of you the report of the commander of the 9th VPS dated the 7th of December, 1991 sent to the head of the First Administration. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be given D45, if I'm not mistaken. Defence Exhibit D45. I'm sorry, D55 is the report. I beg your pardon. I have to apologise once again. It is D65. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, you have read this document, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: -- can we ask for clarification. This an article or is this a report? I'm not clear if we have the correct...

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a report of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector about the action taken by the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Rodic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That document was sent on the 7th of December, 1991 to the First Administration for General Simonovic. General Zorc, can you tell me whether one can infer on the basis of this document whether the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade was indisciplined [as interpreted] and that he should therefore be removed? Can you see that in document? Do you have anything that points to that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier on, you have asked me whether I read this report. Unfortunately not. I did see it earlier on, that is to say, when you put another question to me. But otherwise not. And can, in fact, I draw such a conclusion from this document? Well, I would have to read it first. And if that's important, then I have to read it first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Our time is quite short, if you can -- or let's leave that for the break. And could you now look at page 2 of the document directly. Item 4, does it say that the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade was removed from his position?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That can be seen from item -- point 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that item 4, there is no mention of any removal of the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, bearing in mind the measures taken, could the commander of the 9th VPS have removed the commander of the 3rd Battalion, too, if he deemed it necessary?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that I do not know with what competence he replaced the commander of the 3rd -- the 5th Brigade. I do not know whether this was his authority or that perhaps a superior to his commander would have done so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I believe there may be a transcript error at page 27, line 3. He replaced the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that an error, Mr. Rodic, that you want to correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade. The witness did give an answer. He said that he was removed, as it says in the document. And my question was whether the commander of the 9th VPS could have done the same thing in relation to the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade. So my learned friend's intervention was important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to add, General Zorc, if you could not see from the other documents that this 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade was also subordinated to the commander of the 9th VPS, if that is of any assistance in your conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would indeed because it would be evident that the commander of the 5th Brigade was subordinated to the Military Naval Sector, to the 9th VPS. But I did say that in my opinion, the commander of the sector, in fact, did not have the authority to replace the commander. He could only propose it. Had it been done -- if it was done anyway, well, possibly, then this was a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can put that document aside and then perhaps we'll go back to it a bit later and perhaps you can read it in detail during the break. Tell me, please, the commander of the 9th VPS, could he have received direct orders from the federal secretary for national defence, that he should write him a report or that he should inform him in other ways about the damages and consequences of what happened in Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The federal secretary could have done so, could have ordered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday, you had that report dated the 9th of December, the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector that was sent directly to the deputy federal secretary for national defence, Admiral Brovet. Does this report reflect the answer of the commander of the 9th VPS to the task that he had been given?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The federal secretary could, in fact, transfer or make known this decision through his deputy, General Brovet. And then the answer by the commander of the 9th VPS to Brovet would also be answering the requirement of the federal secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll show you a portion of the interview in order to remind you - you must have read that. That's on page 166 of the B/C/S and page 180 of the English. The investigator's question: "Why did you report directly in this specific case, or directly inform the SSNO, the Federal Secretariat for National Defence?" And the answer by Jokic was: "Well, because I was asked directly by Admiral Brovet to submit such a report without any mediation by the 2nd Operational Group." The investigator's question: "Does that not strike you as unusual?" And the answer is: "This is not regular procedure, but this is usually done to shorten the procedure. This can be done, but the commander is then duty-bound to send a copy of this report to the highest command, and another copy to his own command." When reading the interview, did you come across General -- Admiral Brovet asking this directly from the commander of the 9th VPS? Do you remember this in the report about the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I remember seeing it in the interview, and the report also was shown to me, the report of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, under the assumption that those two had gone to see General Kadijevic in relation to the 6th of December, that they had been summoned, the commander of the operational group and the 9th VPS, could one then assume that from the moment the commander of the 9th VPS was ordered to carry out an investigation into that event which happened on the 6th of December and to send a report on those developments, that the commander of the VPS did so, writing the reports dating the 7 and 9th of December, 1991 respectively?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, sir, if he had sent those reports to Belgrade directly, would the General Staff and the federal secretary for national defence have been informed, both of them, in such a way and could they have taken matters into their hands?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff and the federal secretariat indeed led, controlled all operations of the armed forces. They could have also -- they could have assumed and taken into their hands, in fact, dealing with the whole incidents, but they would have to, in fact, say it to the commanders of the 2nd Operational Group and the 9th VPS, if I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. At any rate, this is how information about the events of the 6th was passed on to the highest command, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll move on to something else now. And I'll ask you the following: First of all, tell me, what is the role of the operational centre at a corps command, the function and role of the operational centre briefly?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to put it very briefly, the operational centre is that part of the command that in interruptedly [as interpreted] 24 hours a day follows up on the position within the scope of responsibility, follows up also the activities if there are activities underway or if the subordinates receive such orders. And also, data are being collected, analysed, then he also suggests urgent measures as well as presentation of reports to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you tell me, please, whether there's a logbook kept at the operational centre where every important information and all important developments are entered? Tell me, as for this important information and developments, it's not the first and primary duty of the operational centre and the team working there to inform their commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the duty operations officer or the duty chief of the operational team, whatever the official name is for that position, is he permanently on duty at the operational centre? What would his role be? I mean specifically the superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the person that is in charge of the work of the centre and sees to it that all links, all connections with operational units, in fact, are ensured. And with the assistance of his assistants, he also follows the intelligence situation, the status of the units, organises also an analysis of data, and also informs the commander. He is the one who is responsible for the work of the operational centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can one go through the operational centre, or rather the duty operations officer, to coordinate the work of the command and to issue orders to subordinate units under that command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The operational centre does not coordinate the work of the command itself at horizontal level. This is done by the Chief of Staff. Through this operational centre, however, all orders to subordinate units can be communicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, the operational centre can convey orders to subordinate units from the corps commander and from the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, if the commander of the 9th VPS, if on the 6th of December, 1991, in the morning at 0445, so if he is informed that an independent battalion under his command, by way of an example the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, has come under fire from Srdj, that one man has been killed and two wounded, and in the eventuality where on the previous day the same commander of the 9th VPS had brokered a cease-fire with the opposite side, if that is the situation, what specifically should he do?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the operational sense, in connection with the action of the 3rd Battalion, I believe that there would be -- it wouldn't be needed that he intervenes personally. I think that the battalion commander could react personally concerning such an eventuality. But if he were the one who brokered the cease-fire and if fire had been opened against his unit and a cease-fire violation occurred, then he personally must first inform the superiors that there was a violation of the cease-fire by the shelling of his units, directed to his units. And I assume that if he was leading negotiations with the other side, he would have to have also connections with the other party and immediately lodge a protest to the other party if something like that happened. Although the mode of reaction will depend also very much on the person himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that is the situation and he receives information, that means a cease-fire had been agreed previously and now he receives word that in one of his units, the 3rd Battalion, a battalion that's subordinated to him, one man has been killed and two wounded, can he at any rate go back to sleep?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a rather sensitive question. Now, in peace, when you hear that a soldier has been killed, it sounds terrible. But in battle, that happens, and more than one are killed. And that doesn't mean that the superior commander or the superior officers will be awake day in and day out, night after night. There's also the operational centre for that. And in peacetime, it's difficult to say. I don't believe that he could sleep because of the very incident -- not the very incident, but not the only the fact that a person was killed and some were injured, but also that the incident occurred. I don't think that he could sleep easily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, same as my colleague has done, I'll put the situation to you in the following way: Imagine that the commander of the VPS, the 9th VPS, spoke to the Croatian side on the 5th of December and agreed on a strategically important cease-fire to be signed the next day, the 6th of December. If at 4.45 a.m. he is informed that in the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade there had been a violation of the cease-fire, one man got killed and two men were wounded, he receives this information. In that case, should the corps commander be concerned also about the jeopardy to the cease-fire that had been brokered to the risk posed to a battalion under his command, and also concerned about a possible reaction by that battalion under his command against the other side?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. It is a matter of concern concerning the completely new situation which is indeed serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When the commander carries out an assessment, or rather I'll show you Admiral Jokic's interview dated September 2003, page 124, that's the bottom of the page, 133 in English. And further 134, the investigator's question is: "When did you wake up?" And the answer is: "Quarter to 5.00. I've gone through all my notes and Kozaric's notes, and what I found there was 0445 in the morning. Kozaric woke me up from Kupari, the forward command post, to tell me that he had received a call from Captain Kovacevic, the commander of the 3rd Battalion, from Brgat. He told him that he had come under heavy artillery fire from Srdj, from Nuncijata, that one of his men had been killed and two wounded." I'll skip the following portion. The Admiral was then asked by the investigator: "4.45 local time?" And the answer was: "That's Central European Time according to Greenwich." And the investigator's question was: "So they woke you up before the attack actually started?" Answer: "Yes, yes." And the question by the investigator: "The attack began at 5.45, didn't it?" The answer: "Yes." "At 5:00?" "No. Oh, yes. Well, all I'm saying is based on the reports. The attack is another thing altogether. What I'm telling you is what the reports said, the reports that I received." And on page 125, that's page 134 in English, at the bottom of the page, I'll just read out the answer to you: "I told Kozaric `monitor the situation, wake me up again if that's what it takes.' At 6.00, he was back calling me over the phone through my assistant officer." And so on and so forth. Did you perhaps notice that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Excuse me, but I think some of the portions that are being skipped, if a whole picture is going to be presented, then counsel selectively excising portions that may well go into the factoring of any possible -- response to any possible question, and it would seem that either the whole line of questioning be put or -- I can certainly wait to do it on redirect, but I think that it doesn't give the witness a view of what's actually been said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have tried to faithfully convey what the interview actually says. And I only skipped some portions in order to save time. The essential thing was about Admiral Jokic waking up and going back to sleep. And I believe that has been faithfully conveyed. If my learned friend has any objections to my interpretation regarding that, please let her say so. Or else, she can deal with that during re-examination. But I'm quite sure that all my interpretations are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The point I want to make, Your Honour, is that what counsel wished to skip, for example, about assessing whatever the situation is, is that: "And Kovacevic told Kozaric, the duty officer, 'now I am leaving the command post at Brgat and going for Zarkovica to see the situation.'" And I think these are facts that indicate that there is still a period of assessment. So the facts are not being conveyed as they have been relayed in the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that has now been dealt with. Part of the problem, Mr. Rodic, may be that you see one line of things as relevant and Ms. Somers another aspect of the same quotation. Between you, no doubt, we will get everything that is thought relevant before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, could you perhaps provide an answer.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that when -- going through the interview of Admiral Jokic, that it seemed that it happened quite early. But as you've noticed from my report, I haven't been asked anything about the concrete situation, the concrete responses of any of the sides. And I didn't go into this because it wasn't relevant for my answers to the questions that were posed to me. But I have noticed it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will also show you his statement on page 153 of the B/C/S and 144 of the English. Investigator's question: "You spoke to Captain Kovacevic before he started the attack. In that conversation, he warned you that he would start the attack, didn't he?" Answer: "No, no. It wasn't me that spoke to him, no. I didn't succeed in speaking to him throughout, not even after my return from Belgrade." Question: "Yes. But Kozaric did speak to him, didn't he?" The Admiral's answer is: "Yes." Question: "And it was Kozaric that informed you that one of your subordinates would start an attack that you had prohibited?" Answer: "Yes, yes." Question: "And then you went back to sleep, and then they woke you up again saying that the attack had begun?" Answer: "Yes." And then adding: "No, no. The first time he called, he told me that the attack would begin. Perhaps I was not clear enough." At any rate, given what the situation was on the ground --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I have to correct my learned friend's reading of it. The English says: "That's right. No, I was not clear on that point. She did not say the first time that the attack was to be put in."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, General Zorc, could you please tell us, given the situation on the 6th of December, would it have been reasonable at all for a corps commander who was responsible to go back to sleep, having received such crucial information?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be difficult to give an affirmative answer. This is a possible reaction of a responsible officer. However, as a personal situation, a psychophysical condition, all this influences, and therefore I would not dare evaluate and judge whether his action was correct or not. If it was wise or not. If he was psychologically and physically fit, he should have reacted and prevented the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll try to simplify this. In the situation that I just described to you in relation to the 6th of December, the unit where some soldiers got killed or wounded, these developments in terms of their importance, would have not they constituted sufficient reason to alert all elements of command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, particularly of his command. Because the command, the operational centre, the Chiefs of Staff, all they are the factors which allow the commander also to take a rest. But once the information came in that shelling will take place, something which has been banned, then that is cause for alerting the entire command and control system which should prevent such a situation, or if it already began, to stop it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The commander of the 9th VPS, or rather, his command, was it not their duty to inform their superior command about this, in this case, the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll now show you what Admiral Jokic said in his interview, B/C/S 126, and the end of page 135 in the English. The investigator's question: "Was the 2nd Operational Group immediately informed about the intentions of Kovacevic's battalion?" Answer: "No, no, no. Not then." Question: "And why not?" Answer: "Well, I had more urgent business to deal with, to stop the attack. For me, the priority was to stop the captain from doing anything silly." In this way, was the rule about informing one's superior command about urgent situations and urgent developments complied with?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how this occurred in that situation, I don't know. But such a situation as you explained to me would be indeed a surprise for me; namely, also personally, if I were faced with such a situation, I would have as a priority to prevent or stop the shelling. However, the reporting, informing of the superior is carried out through my command and operations centre, and this can be done in parallel or even before that. So it's not one or the other, but simultaneously both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please specify, the corps commander, would it have been his duty to inform the command of the 2nd Operational Group about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander is responsible for informing the superior command. And he does this through the operational centre and his command without the need of a special -- issuing a special order. This is combat activity which has to be reported upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If there's a strategically important cease-fire with the opposite side at stake, would it not be usual for the commander of the military naval sector, would it not be usual for the commander of the military naval sector, his Chief of Staff, his assistant for land forces who was exercising control over the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to be 50 kilometres away from the forward command post? Would that have been a responsible thing to do, to leave none of these important officers at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If at the forward command post there is no one, then it doesn't exist. If a forward command post is not a fundamental -- the fundamental is the command post. The forward command post is temporary, and the commander is there to supervise the main activities of his subordinate unit. The fact whether he is reacting from the forward or the basic command post, that is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, if the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector on the 6th of December, in the morning, at 6.50, for example, was informed that his 3rd Battalion is out to attack Srdj, although they do not have orders for any such thing, what is the commander of the 9th VPS supposed to do then?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the unit is activated, although there isn't no such assignment, then he should stop such an activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If after such information, namely, that his unit is out to attack, if he then issued an order to the duty operations officer to convey his order to forbid the attack, and if that order was not carried out, is it possible that if shelling occurs, as shelling did occur of the town of Dubrovnik, is it possible that it is first the federal secretary in Belgrade who finds out about this and that the commander of the 9th VPS finds out about this only when the federal secretary informs him about this through the commander of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but this is possible. The means of communication were at the time when this was happening, the civilian means of communication were faster than the military ones. And it's a question of electronic communication, and it's possible that the entire world hears about it before he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer to my military question moved into the area of communications. But let me help you. If all communications are working, that is to say, telephones and radio communications, between the commander, his forward command post, and the Dubrovnik side, what then? What do you say then to the previous question?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information concerning -- along the chain of command must be the speediest and prompt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. But for the transcript, let us clarify one thing in this chain of command. Should this information go from the top or from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the subordinate units upwards, along the chain of command, the line of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, after receiving a warning from the federal secretary and the commander of the 2nd Operational Group about this incident, and also after having received orders to stop the attack, is it then in the spirit of the rules of command and control for the commander of the 9th VPS, that is to say, would it be in the spirit of the rules, that the commander of the 9th VPS would not inform the commander of the 2nd Operational Group about developments in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Concerning all events in the unit, the sector command must regularly inform the command of the operational group, irrespective of different reasons from where the information is arriving or anything similar. If the sector commander received a special order from the federal secretary for a certain action, namely, that the shelling be stopped, if he received this directly, he would first have to convey this order to the subordinate units; and through the operational centre, inform about it his direct superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If in the area of responsibility and operations of the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector the town of Dubrovnik is included and its surrounding area and within Dubrovnik the Old Town as a protected monument, is it possible that after the intervention of the federal secretary for national defence who called him to come to Belgrade, is it possible in that situation that the commander of the 9th VPS does not investigate whether there was any shelling of the Old Town and if he were cautioned about this by the representatives of the other side, the Dubrovnik people?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I must say that certain activities occur in parallel. The commander generally doesn't carry out the activities alone, individually. He can't do that. Therefore, on the basis of the rules, the provisions, in view of the fact that unlawful shelling occurred, which is also against the orders he issued to his subordinates, he must ensure that the incident be investigated, and he must inform the superior command. This investigation is carried out by the bodies of his command, by the staff. Now, the question whether he personally must get involved in the investigation of the incident or answer to the superior, namely, the national -- federal secretary, and that he come to Belgrade, that is a particularly dilemma and a question of subordination. But of course, in such a situation, he should have the understanding of the federal secretary for postponing the meeting while the investigation is taking place and highlighting the various aspects of the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector sends four of his high-ranking officers, four colonels, including the Chief of Staff of the 9th Military Naval Sector to stop this attack, and if his order is not carried out, that is to say, if this attack continues in spite of his orders, is the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector supposed to go out himself to try to stop this personally?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I wrote in my report and as I have answered a number of times concerning similar questions, personally he, the commander, gets personally involved when, with all other means, orders via his representatives, he does not succeed in achieving and implementing his decision. In this case, this would be the stopping of the shelling. Of course, the fact, the very fact that he cannot achieve this through his representatives and his deputy is unusual and regrettable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the commander of the 9th VPS does not have a direct link with his four high-ranking officers, the ones he sent to stop the attack, and if he does not have a direct link with the commander of the battalion, the 3rd Battalion, that is out attacking, what could he do in the least? Wouldn't it be for him to go to the forward command post from where he could have this direct link?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, again, we are again dealing with a means of communication. Now, if the commander from anywhere in his zone doesn't have a line of communication with his command, with the subordinates, and subordinate officers, then he couldn't use these means even from a forward command post. Regrettably, in such a situation when the communication lines are severed or don't exist or are not of suitable quality, nothing else remains to him but to go personally. Not only to the forward command post, but also directly to the unit that is involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Perhaps I'm exhausting you with this, but I would like to put to you some other elements related to this situation. If the commander of the 9th VPS is 8 kilometres away from the forward command post and 12 kilometres away from where the battalion commander is, the one who's carrying out the attack, does this distance constitute a problem, any kind of problem, for going to the forward command post or the command post of the 3rd Battalion in that critical situation?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the distance itself in the case of a commander of a VPS represents almost no distance at all, presuming, of course, he has the necessary means of transportation. And of course, presuming that the tactical situation allows him to move around the battle area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if he can travel, if he does have a vehicle, then he should go to the two mentioned places because such a distance is not a problem. Did I understand you correctly? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me correctly. This should not have been a problem. His problem was most probably in the simultaneous request for him to appear in Belgrade at that same time, if that was known to him then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, if the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector was informed at 4.45 a.m. about the incident in the 3rd Battalion, that is to say, the killing of one soldier and the wounding of three soldiers, and if at 6.50 a.m. on December 6th he was informed about the attack, and if all the way up to 1400 hours, or rather 1415 hours, he does not have any information or confirmation that his order to stop the attack had been carried out, what does he do then within that time span, from 9.00 -- or rather, from 7.00 o'clock onwards? Did he -- was he supposed to go out and try to stop the attack himself? I'm sorry. In the English interpretation of my question, it says "within that time span." Of nine hours or seven hours, within these nine or seven hours, was the commander supposed to go and try to stop the attack himself personally? Is that time sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.
